 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner in the above writ petition under Article 226 seeks to circumvent the proceedings under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 on the basis of alleged discrepancies in Ext.P1 and P4.
2.

Admittedly, food sample was taken from the petitioner's business premises and on analysis by the Food Analyst, Ext.P1 report was issued, which indicates that the said sample contains an added synthetic food colour, which was not permitted in the said food.

The petitioner filed an appeal under Section 46(4) of the Act, and the certificate of Analysis by Ext.P4 found the presence of Monosodium Glutamate; which as per the prescription made under the Act, should not be present in the food item.

3. The petitioner relies on two decisions of the Delhi High Court produced as Ext.P5 to contend that prosecution should not be initiated and this Court should set aside the certiorari issuance of Ext.P1 and P4 issued respectively by the Public Analyst and the Central Food Laboratory.

4. Primarily it is to be noticed that the decisions referred by the petitioner arise from orders in which the discharge was claimed before the Jurisdictional Magistrate under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Since alternative remedies are available; this Court is not inclined to involve the extraordinary remedy under Article 226.

The writ petition would stand dismissed leaving open the contentions of the petitioner and without making any observations on merits or the applicability of Ext.P5 judgments in the facts of the above case.
The same would have to be urged before the appropriate Court at the appropriate time.
Writ petition would stand dismissed in limine.

Sd/-
 (K. VINOD CHANDRAN, JUDGE)
